name: Dull Blue
lede: Dull Blue is a muted, mid-toned slate blue named by the 2010 xkcd color survey, common enough to turn up in a Monet sunset and a Fra Angelico Madonna alike.

sections.title: A crowd name for a grayed blue
sections.body:
The only recorded source for Dull Blue is the xkcd survey of 2010, following the plain modifier grammar *dull* plus [[blue]] [1]. At hex #49759C it measures lightness 48 and chroma 26 in LCH, and the nearest ISCC-NBS block reads as a moderate blue, 4.8 units off [1].

Its closest named neighbor is [[flat-blue|Flat Blue]], 2.5 units away and more vivid, followed by [[virgin|Stormy Blue]], 2.8 units off and almost the same color [2]. [[queen-blue|Queen Blue]] sits 3.9 units away, also almost the same [2].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds this blue in 76 of 23,781 paintings, about 0.32 percent, as photographed [3]. The earliest match is Fra Angelico's *Madonna of the Pomegranate*, from 1426, 584 years before the xkcd survey fixed the name, a floor and not a first, since the archive's early centuries are thin [3]. It peaks in the 1910s, in 8 of 523 paintings, nearly 5 times the archive's overall rate, with Claude Monet carrying it in 3 of his 50 works here, over 18 times the baseline, including a 1903 view of the Houses of Parliament at sunset [3]. These are screen matches on photographs of varnished paintings, not a record of any pigment [3].
